The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic secant function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arsech}⁡x)=-\frac{1}{x\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\,[-3\,\operatorname{arsech}⁡(2x)] \\  & =-3\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\,[\operatorname{arsech}⁡(2x)] \\  & =-3\cdot [-\frac{1}{2x\sqrt{1-(2x)^{2}}}]\cdot (2x)^{′} \\  & =\frac{3}{2x\sqrt{1-4{x}^{2}}}\cdot 2 \\  & =\frac{3}{x\sqrt{1-4{x}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$
